No generic presentations or theoretical concepts, but intensive workshops built around your own code and business cases. service.processes.title: AI-native business processes

kata.tour.title: What the kata is
kata.tour.body: One day in a real codebase, learning step by step to direct an agent on code that already exists. Like a kata, you learn the movement by repeating it: every exercise builds on the code from the step before. The repository is the lesson, and at the end the build decides whether what came out is good enough.
kata.tour.accents: The course material, the code and the assignments are one whole, and they stay available after the training day. Every page yields the slide the trainer puts on screen, so what you read back later is exactly what you saw that day. The same pages carry a self-study track, in Dutch and English, so you keep building at your own pace and take your colleagues along. The trainers work this way themselves every day: they are not only in front of the room, they sit beside you at the screen.
kata.tour.videoLabel: Tour of the SmartAgents agentic engineering kata
kata.day.lede: The steps build on one another. Where an agent's answer comes from, through to what changes in your own role.
kata.step.00.title: Start here
kata.step.00.body: How the kata works, how to run the project on your own machine, and a first flag board: codes you earn with a solution that works.
kata.step.00.units: How this kata works · The backend · Workshop
kata.step.01.title: Context, model, mechanisms
kata.step.01.body: Where an agent's answer comes from: what is in the context window, what each layer costs and what happens when it fills up.
kata.step.01.units: Tokens · Your prompt · Tools · Context · The session · The harness · The model · Truth · Workshop · Recap
kata.step.02.title: Agentic engineering
kata.step.02.body: How you work with an agent rather than against one. The longest step of the day, and the afternoon workshop sits in it.
kata.step.02.units: Project evolution · Project setup · Craft · Steering · Recurring patterns · Workflows · What it asks of you · Parallel workflows · Spending tokens · Workshop
kata.step.03.title: Soft skills
kata.step.03.body: The part that is not about code: what changes about the work itself, and about how you talk about it.
kata.step.03.units: Change management · Expectation management · Impostor syndrome
kata.practice.title: How you practise
kata.practice.lede: By doing. Most steps carry a flag board: short codes that only surface once you run the code on your own machine, instrument it or harden it. They are nowhere in the text and a search will not find them. The quizzes beside them run in the browser and keep working with the service down. In the afternoon workshop the build decides: coverage, complexity and mutation testing say whether your code is ready, not the agent's word for it.
kata.themes.title: What sticks
kata.themes.lede: Every theme has an exercise behind it where you do it yourself, and every one of them comes back in the work the day after.
kata.theme.truth.title: Truth
kata.theme.truth.body: You know how to check whether an answer is actually right, and where an agent stays quiet about what it guessed.
kata.theme.workflow.title: Workflow
kata.theme.workflow.body: You choose per task how to hand work over: free prompting, a plan, a spec or an audit.
kata.theme.cost.title: Cost
kata.theme.cost.body: You see what is in your context window, turn one interaction into money and know where the tokens go.
kata.theme.setup.title: Setup
kata.theme.setup.body: You set the repository up with instructions, skills, hooks and scripts that come along in every session, so you do not type the same correction five times.
kata.theme.parallel.title: Parallel
kata.theme.parallel.body: You put several agents to work at once, each in its own worktree, and find that your attention runs out before your tokens do.
kata.theme.team.title: Team
kata.theme.team.body: You name what changes about your role, what you may and may not promise, and how you bring everyone else along.

kata.requirement.knowledge.body: Programming experience, your own laptop with the IDE you know, and the rights to install tooling on it locally: the project runs on your own machine.
kata.requirement.tools.title: AI tools
kata.requirement.tools.body: A working installation of Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI: an agent you run in a terminal. The kata starts at tokens and context, so experience with agents is welcome but not required.

staffing.title: AI staffing and coaching · SmartAgents
staffing.description: An AI-native engineer working inside your project, coaching for your developers and AI workflows for your business teams. One track per team, picked on what is stuck today.
staffing.hero.title: An AI-native engineer in your team
staffing.cta.tracks: See how we work with you
staffing.tracks.title: How we work with you
staffing.track.engineer.title: AI engineer staffing
staffing.track.engineer.body: We put an AI-native engineer in your project. They work inside your sprints, your repository and your review, and build up the automation around the code with you, handing over to your own engineers from day one.
staffing.track.engineer.how: In practice: joining the daily stand-up, tickets from the same backlog, pull requests checked by your own reviewers. We configure agents for your codebase, document agreements in the repository and build the gates into your CI/CD, so what we leave behind keeps working without us. You decide on every commit; we are not a black box throwing code over the wall.
staffing.track.engineer.fit: Your project is running, there is work enough, and nobody on the team gets AI further than the search bar.
staffing.track.developers.title: Coaching for developers
staffing.track.developers.body: We teach your engineers to work with AI by doing it together: explaining, demonstrating and applying it to their own tickets, until it sticks.
staffing.track.developers.how: In practice: half a day a week beside your developers, on their own tickets. We work at the same screen, show what an agent can and cannot carry, and set up together the async workflows that keep work moving outside office hours. What we set up is yours and lives in your repository, not in our notes.
staffing.track.developers.fit: Your developers already use AI to complete code, but taking a ticket from start to finish is still no faster.
staffing.track.business.title: Coaching for business teams
staffing.track.business.body: We train your employees ourselves: what AI can and cannot do, and how to put it on their own case files. Coaching alongside the work already on their desk, with repeatable patterns instead of one-off prompts.
staffing.track.business.how: In practice: sessions with the people who do the work, on their own files. We map out together which step AI takes over and which it does not, write that down as a workflow your team runs again, and stay until it runs without us. Not a prompt library, a way of working.
staffing.track.business.fit: Your teams already use AI, each on their own, and nobody can say what is actually being gained.
staffing.cta.title: Looking for someone who already does this?
staffing.cta.body: Tell us briefly where your team is stuck and what the project looks like today. We propose the track that fits.
processes.title: AI-native business processes · SmartAgents
processes.description: We go through the work your teams do today, say where AI pays off and where it does not, and leave reusable workflows, skills and agents behind. With coaching until your people run them.
processes.hero.title: From your tasks to reusable workflows
processes.phases.title: How an engagement runs
processes.phases.lede: We take one process that comes back every week and follow it end to end. Not a drawing on paper, but the work that is on the table this week, gone through with your own people. We also say where AI adds nothing.
processes.phase.01.title: Going through the work
processes.phase.01.body: In the SmartScan we walk through the tasks on the table this week with your people: mail, quotes, reporting, case files. Not what the process is supposed to be, but what actually happens.
processes.phase.02.title: Where AI pays off
processes.phase.02.body: Task by task we say where AI takes the work over, where it only assists, and where it adds nothing. That last one is almost always part of the answer.
processes.phase.03.title: Making it reusable
processes.phase.03.body: We build what keeps coming back: a workflow your team runs again, a skill that captures your way of working, an agent that handles a piece on its own.
processes.phase.04.title: Coaching until it runs
processes.phase.04.body: We work on your own case files, alongside the people who do that work every day, until they run the new workflow without us.
processes.outcome.title: What you keep
processes.outcome.workflows.title: Workflows
processes.outcome.workflows.body: The work that comes back every week, set down as steps your team runs again next week, with the same outcome.
processes.outcome.skills.title: Skills
processes.outcome.skills.body: Your templates, your house rules and the way you phrase things, captured so nobody has to explain them again at every request.
processes.outcome.agents.title: Agents
processes.outcome.agents.body: For the work nobody needs to do by hand anymore: an agent that handles the task and involves you when a decision is needed.
processes.outcome.people.title: People who use them
processes.outcome.people.body: The colleagues who do the work run the new workflow themselves. If something stays untouched, it does not belong in the process and it goes.
processes.cta.title: Which process shall we go through?
processes.cta.body: Tell us briefly what work comes back every week and who does it today. We propose where we would start, and we also say when AI adds nothing to it.
sdlc.title: AI-native SDLC · SmartAgents
sdlc.description: From an SDLC with six desks and five handoffs to an AI-native one with four gates. We guide software teams through that shift: most of the work is not technical but human.
sdlc.hero.title: From traditional SDLC to AI-native
sdlc.issues.title: What we see today
sdlc.issue.belief.title: Belief
sdlc.issue.belief.body: Part of the team dismisses AI before trying it, and another part expects miracles. That is the same mistake in two directions.
sdlc.issue.capability.title: Capability
sdlc.issue.capability.body: No training, too little access to AI tooling, and processes built for a world where writing code was the expensive part.
sdlc.issue.foundation.title: Foundation
sdlc.issue.foundation.body: Most product knowledge lives in people's heads. AI workflows are fragmented, each only as good as whoever built it.
sdlc.issue.tooling.title: Adoption
sdlc.issue.tooling.body: The spread between teams is huge: some work almost AI-first, others barely use AI. There is no common way of working to close that gap.
sdlc.journey.title: The way there
sdlc.journey.lede: We build on what Anthropic publishes about AI-native engineering. The bottleneck does not disappear, it moves: in the end, to the moment someone decides.
sdlc.stage.today.title: Today
sdlc.stage.today.body: Six desks, five handoffs. Build takes the longest, and it sets the pace for the whole chain.
sdlc.stage.ungated.title: AI-assisted
sdlc.stage.ungated.body: Agents build. The bottleneck moves to what you asked for and to whoever checks it.
sdlc.stage.native.title: AI-native
sdlc.stage.native.body: One run, no handoffs. A person still decides four times, and that is the only thing still holding the work up.
sdlc.gates.label: Four gates
sdlc.loop.label: What happens in production feeds the next piece of work
sdlc.legend.flow: Where the run narrows, the work waits
sdlc.work.title: Where the real work is
sdlc.work.lede: Most of this is not technical. It is bringing people along, and building a way of working on the culture and the habits you already have.
sdlc.work.people.title: Bringing people along
sdlc.work.people.body: “We have always done it this way” is not answered by a memo. We put someone in the team who has already made the move, and show the difference in a real repository, against what the team would have shipped itself.
sdlc.work.culture.title: Built on your own culture
sdlc.work.culture.body: There is no standard process we come and install. We start from how your teams work today and from what already works well, and build on that.
sdlc.work.training.title: Training
sdlc.work.training.body: People who use AI every day still ask us what MCP is, use the agent as a search box, and point it at small chores instead of at whole workflows. The willingness is there, the knowledge is not yet. We train your engineers on agentic workflows, not on one-off prompts.
sdlc.work.gates.title: Quality gates
sdlc.work.gates.body: We build quality gates into your CI/CD, so quality becomes visible and automatic, and every team holds to today’s standards, or stricter. Nobody reviews by hand the volume an agent produces: the quality gates take the volume, your reviewers judge the decisions. Access without gates buys you more code and less confidence in it.
sdlc.work.platform.title: One way of working
sdlc.work.platform.body: We help a small platform team of your own set the agreements down in the repository and carry them into every team through the tooling itself, not through a wiki page written once and never read again. It is a baseline, not a limit: each team builds on it, and feedback from every team adjusts it.
sdlc.cta.title: Where does your team stand today?
sdlc.cta.body: Tell us briefly how your teams work today and where it is rubbing. We say which step comes first, and why it comes first.
team.title: Team · SmartAgents
team.description: The people behind SmartAgents: Axel Segers and Tom Haeldermans, the two founders of an agency that builds digital colleagues for Belgian organisations.
team.hero.title: Meet our team
team.person.axel.body: Entrepreneur with more than 25 years of experience in digital transformation. Helps organisations discover where intelligent automation can make a difference.
team.person.tom.body: Technical architect specialised in agentic AI systems and automation at enterprise scale. Builds solutions that scale and keep working.
team.story.title: Our origin
team.story.1: Almost every company we spoke to ran into the same thing: real enthusiasm for AI, but no idea where to start. Plenty of pilots and standalone tools stalled after a promising launch.
team.story.2: That is why we started SmartAgents. No vague presentations about what's possible, but solutions that are already running the week after. We only recommend tooling we test and use daily on our own projects, so we know exactly what works and, more importantly, what does not.
team.cta.title: Shall we get to know each other?
team.cta.body: Tell us briefly what could run better. You get one of the two of us at the table.
